question: Which Indian author wrote the novel Midnight's Children, which won the Booker Prize?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Salman Rushdie**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The novel **Midnight's Children** was written by the world-renowned author **Salman Rushdie** and was published in the year **1981**.
 
• The book is a classic example of **magical realism** and **postcolonial literature**, weaving historical events of **India** with fictional elements.
 
• The story revolves around **Saleem Sinai**, who is born at the exact moment of **India's Independence** at midnight on **August 15, 1947**. Hence, the statement that Salman Rushdie is the author is correct.
 
• The novel was awarded the prestigious **Booker Prize** in **1981**. It later achieved the unique distinction of winning the **"Booker of Bookers"** in **1993** and **"The Best of the Booker"** in **2008** to celebrate the **25th** and **40th** anniversaries of the prize, respectively.
